tldr: For a prespecified designated programme versus the uniformly averaged alternative menu on a binary endpoint, the unrestricted finite-population minimax improvement has the uniform scale \(d(n,m)\asymp\max\{m^{-2/3}n^{-4/3},n^{-3/2}\}\), with explicit constants \(3/1024\) and \(64\), no logarithms, and validity for every \(n\geq2,m\geq1\). Independent contrast-weighted assignment with a total clipped-or-affine estimator attains the bound; a compatible complete-schedule prior proves the converse against every dependent nonadaptive design and every full-label randomized estimator. Writing \(a_{\rm aff}(n)=n^{-1}-(1+\sqrt n)^{-2}\), the ratio \(d(n,m)/a_{\rm aff}(n)\) diverges for \(m=o(n^{1/4})\) and is uniformly bounded above and below whenever \(m\) is bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of \(n^{1/4}\). The matched growing-menu frontier is the contribution; the fixed-menu order, uniform first-order benchmark, and affine baseline remain credited prior art.
